title: Important JavaScript Runtime Concepts knowledge check

questions.prompt: What must be true for a TypeScript import to work in an application?
options: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
The compiler always rewrites every alias into a working runtime path.
Any filename extension works with every runtime.
Type-only imports create runtime values automatically.
questions.answer_key: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
questions.explanation: Type checking and runtime module loading are related but distinct responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Important JavaScript Runtime Concepts”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with reference values and identity and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with reference values and identity and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Reference values and identity”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Important JavaScript Runtime Concepts”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check closures and lexical scope, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume prototype-based inheritance and this is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check closures and lexical scope, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Closures and lexical scope”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
